body.x: AiM Future Inc. (CEO Chang-soo Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

AiM Future is an NeuroMosAlc architecture-based NPU (Neural Processing Unit) IP developer. With their focus being on the development of efficient AI hardware for the processing of artificial intelligence networks, the startup currently pursues business models such as NPU IP development, AI algorithm development and optimization, and AI chip and AI system manufacturing.

Their main products include both hardware and software, the NeuroMosAlc Processor and NeuroMosAlc Studio, respectively. Based on these offerings, the tech company aims to become a comprehensive AI solution provider in the Internet of Things (IoT), consumer electronics, AR & VR, and drone robotics markets.

In this exhibition, AiM Future presented the NeuroMosaic Hardware Processor, its NPU IP, along with other products. They provide hardware with various options based on the two-stage hierarchy of Tile and Tilelet. The system is embedded with up to 8 tiles and 16 tilelets per tile.

Also, the hardware’s upper tier tile operates as a memory controller capable of three-dimensional data shaping, whereas the lower tier tilelet functions as a high-performing NPU for efficient artificial intelligence calculations. This scalable hardware structure can be applied to various application groups, and its performance is maximized when linked with AiM Future software that supports artificial intelligence frameworks such as Caffe, TensorFlow, and PyTourch.

According to a representative from AiM Future, “We plan to leverage this CES to actively network with other enterprises to promote us and our technology.” They added, “On top of that, we hope to get various feedback for improvements. This will help us to identify markets and technical trends as well as collect information about new applications.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
